acceptance_criteria: AC1: `layoutNeighborhood` places every first-step neighbour whose only edges with the root point at the root left of the root, every neighbour the root points at right of it, and no two laid-out boxes (nodes, group captions, overflow entries) overlap, for a 31-node depth-1 projection of mixed `contains` and `imports` edges. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/graphLayout.test.ts`]

AC2: When a side has more neighbours than the column cap of 12, the layout shows exactly 12 nodes in that column plus one overflow entry whose hidden count equals that side's neighbour count minus 12; a 200-node, 269-edge depth-2 projection lays out with no overlapping boxes and at most 12 nodes per column. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/graphLayout.test.ts`]

AC3: Every second-step node is placed in the outer column on the side of the first-step node it is attached to, further from the root than every first-step node on that side. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/graphLayout.test.ts`]

AC4: `RelationshipGraph` renders an HTML caption with the root title and the incoming and outgoing counts (and the word "limited" for a truncated projection) and an HTML legend that names, with human-readable labels, exactly the node kinds and line styles present in the projection; the style mapping is a pure exported function that gives each of the seven node kinds a distinct shape-or-border treatment and maps the nine relationship kinds onto solid, dashed and dotted lines. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/RelationshipGraph.dom.test.tsx`]

AC5: In the browser dev build at a 1180×780 window with the details panel open, graph node labels render at 9 px or more and no two nodes overlap, both for a module with at least 30 neighbours at depth 1 and for a 200-node projection at depth 2 (measured on the live cytoscape instance: label font size × zoom, and node bounding boxes). [verify: judged]

AC6: Changing `data-theme` or `data-palette` on the document element re-colours the mounted graph without a selection change: after the switch the label colour equals the new theme's `--fg`. [verify: judged]

AC7: `NodeDetailsPanel` shows the selected node's kind as a text badge, its title, its repository path with a "Copy path" control that writes the path to the clipboard, and "N incoming · M outgoing" counts computed from the root-adjacent edges of the `relationships` projection, with "limited" when it is truncated. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/NodeDetailsPanel.dom.test.tsx`]

AC8: Relationships is the default tab and lists root-adjacent relationships grouped by direction and then relationship kind; activating a row calls `onSelect` with that neighbour's id; relationships between two non-root nodes are listed in a separate group whose rows can open either endpoint; a change of `revealRelationships` switches to the Relationships tab. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/NodeDetailsPanel.dom.test.tsx src/metaproject/RelationshipList.dom.test.tsx`]

AC9: A linked-document preview contains no Markdown markers and skips metadata: for a page whose body starts with a `> **Covers:**` blockquote line followed by a prose paragraph, the preview is that prose paragraph with no `>`, `**`, emphasis underscores or backticks. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/NodeDetailsPanel.dom.test.tsx`]

AC10: Explorer state survives leaving the work view: in the browser dev build, after selecting a node in Graph with a non-empty query and the panel open, switching to Flows and back shows the same view, query, selection, filters, open panel and an available Back button. [verify: judged]

AC11: Back steps through in-view navigation: after selecting nodes A, then B, then C in Graph, Back shows B and Back again shows A; typing in the search field adds no history entries. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]

AC12: "Find a Wiki page" for a node with no matching page shows, in the article area, an empty state that names the searched text, and renders no wiki article. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]

AC13: The Wiki view's relationships read does not depend on Graph filter state: with Graph depth set to 2 and a relationship type unticked, the neighbours request issued in Wiki mode has depth 1, direction "both" and every non-symbol relationship kind. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]

AC14: A rebuild never leaves its control stuck: when the catalog is reloaded while a rebuild is in flight, then after the rebuild resolves successfully the "Rebuild graph" control is enabled again and the catalog is read again. · sensitive: failure-scenario [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]

AC15: A failed protocol negotiation is recoverable: the error is shown with a Retry control and without "Loading project knowledge…"; activating Retry negotiates again and, on success, loads the catalog. · sensitive: failure-scenario [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]

[verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]

conduct: Agent conduct (mandatory): (1) No AI attribution: no `Co-Authored-By:` trailer or "Generated by/with …" line naming an AI model, agent or tool in commit messages, PR or ticket descriptions, or comments. A human co-author, a code-generator note and a model name as technical provenance are allowed. (2) No commit, push, merge or release without an explicit ask. Invoking an orchestrator is the ask for its own task-boundary commits; merge and release always need their own ask. (3) Never destroy others' work: no `git stash` in a dirty tree, no blanket `git add -A` while parallel lanes share a checkout, no force-push to a shared branch. (4) No secrets or personal data in output, logs or commits. (5) Report honestly: name what failed, what was skipped and what was not verified.

finding.quote: .metaproject-filters-pop { display: grid; gap: var(--sp-2); padding: var(--sp-2) var(--sp-3) var(--sp-3); }
finding.problem: Filters popover is clipped by 51 px at the 720x480 minimum window when the stale banner is expanded, and cannot scroll. The popover is a fixed-position .menu whose top is computed once as anchor.bottom + 4 (MetaprojectView.tsx FiltersPopover: `setPosition({ left, top: rect.bottom + 4 })`). The only height limit is the shared .menu max-block-size of 400px, a fixed number, not a function of the room below the anchor. The rule above adds no max-block-size or overflow clamp tied to the window, so when the anchor sits low the popover runs past the window edge. Its content (229 px) is below 400 px, so it never becomes scrollable either and the last row is unreachable.
finding.impact: At the smallest supported window (720x480), a developer with a stale graph who opens Details and then Filters cannot reach the lower relationship-type chips, the symbol-layer reason or Reset filters. A stale graph is the state the flow journal calls the one a developer is in most of the time. Any state that pushes the header down further (a longer reason, a second banner, a larger text scale) moves the cut up. The position is computed once on open, so a resize while it is open is not tracked (unmeasured).
finding.suggested_fix: Bound the popover by the room below its anchor: compute `maxHeight = window.innerHeight - top - 8` next to `top` in FiltersPopover and set `max-block-size: min(400px, that)` with `overflow-y: auto`; or flip it above the anchor when there is more room there. Re-measure at 720x480 with Details expanded: popover bottom at or below 472 and scrollHeight greater than clientHeight.
finding.evidence: Orchestrator live probe, browser dev build, 720x480, dark, Graph, 'Agent Bus', depth 1, getBoundingClientRect (research-evidence/live-filters-popover-720x480.txt). One-line banner: button bottom 225, popover top 232 bottom 455, 25 px of room, not cut. Banner with Details expanded (banner 122 px): button bottom 301, popover top 308 bottom 531, window 480, cut by 51 px; scrollHeight equals clientHeight (229), so no scroll; the 'Not available: ...' note and the lower chips are outside the window. Not measured: light theme, 1180x780 and 1440x900 with the popover open, the native Tauri window, window resize while open. Measured by the orchestrator in two engines at 720x480 with the freshness Details expanded: Chromium 156, popover bottom 531 against a 480 px window, cut by 51 px, no scroll (.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-branch/research-evidence/live-filters-popover-720x480.txt); system WKWebView (AppleWebKit 605.1.15, macOS 26.7.3), layout box bottom 497, cut by 17 px, no scroll (.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-branch/research-evidence/verify-F-001-3.txt). With the one-line banner it fits in both (.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-branch/research-evidence/verify-F-001-2.txt). The height cap the reviewer calls max-block-size 400px is `.menu`'s `max-height: min(420px, calc(100vh - 80px))` (styles.css:143), which is 400 px at this window height. Normalisation notes: confidence was not stated by the reviewer and is set at normalisation; the same defect was raised by review-ui-ux (review-ui-ux-w2, UX-001, minor); the same defect was raised by review-ui-ux (review-ui-ux-w1, UX-002, info).

finding.problem: FiltersPopover registers on the app-wide Escape stack (components/ui.tsx:44-70: window keydown listener, `e.preventDefault(); top.current?.()` for the top entry) and so makes `overlayOpen()` true (ui.tsx:81). On base the explorer was unmounted when the user left the view, taking any popover with it. On head the explorer is mounted but hidden (RetainedView), and `filtersOpen` is deliberately kept across view switches (comment 'Open or closed is explorer state ... survives a view or tab switch'). The only close paths are Escape, a mousedown outside, or the button. A keyboard user can Tab to the sidebar nav and press Enter (no mousedown, popover has no focus-out close) and arrive in another view with the popover open but hidden.
finding.impact: While that hidden popover is registered: the first Escape in the other view is consumed by it (preventDefault, then focuses a hidden anchor), so Escape does not reach the visible view; AppShell's view shortcuts back off (AppShell.tsx:84 and :112 return when overlayOpen()); App.tsx:360 and BrowserPanel.tsx:114 (`show = ... && !overlayOpen()`) also treat an overlay as open, so the native browser view hides. Nothing on screen explains it; a second Escape clears it. If true for you: minor (recoverable, needs the keyboard path described).
finding.suggested_fix: Close the popover when its view is hidden: pass the RetainedView `visible` flag into MetaprojectView and call setFiltersOpen(false) on becoming hidden, or mount FiltersPopover only while visible. Add a test that switches view with the popover open and checks overlayOpen() is false.
finding.evidence: Also described, without a finding, by review-regression (wave 2), which lists the overlayOpen() consumers it reaches: App.tsx:360, AppShell.tsx:84/112, BrowserPanel.tsx:114/130, ReviewBoard.tsx:247/258. Normalisation notes: the same defect was raised by review-highload (review-highload-w2, F-001, minor); the same defect was raised by review-frontend (review-frontend-w2, its unnumbered finding, info); the same defect was raised by review-logic (review-logic-w5, F-001, minor).

finding.problem:
Base: `{workView === "metaproject" &&

finding.quote: const current = () => generation === project.current && shownSelection.current === from && activeMode.current === "wiki";
finding.problem: Concurrent wiki-link lookups are won by whichever read returns first
finding.impact: Trigger: click an unloaded wiki link A, then another unloaded link B on the same page before A's `search` read resolves. Both reads pass `current()` because the selection has not changed; whichever resolves first calls `openDocument` and changes the selection, after which the other is dropped. If A's read is the slower one, B opens (the last click wins); if A is faster, A opens and B is silently discarded. The outcome depends on read latency, not click order. No data is lost and the user can click again.
finding.suggested_fix: Keep a lookup counter in a ref, increment it in openPath, and have `current()` also require `token === lookup.current` (the pattern `latestSearch.current.generation` already uses nearby).
finding.evidence: `const current = () => generation === project.current && shownSelection.current === from && activeMode.current === "wiki";` in openPath, which guards only against a changed project, selection or mode, not against a second lookup started from the same page. Normalisation notes: confidence was not stated by the reviewer and is set at normalisation; the quote was taken at normalisation from the code the reviewer cited.

finding.problem: Recorded OpenSpec scroll defect still live: choose() zeroes the content pane before the history entry is recorded. T7's result lists under noticed_not_touched that OpenSpecView choose() sets the content scrollTop to 0 before calling onLocation, so the entry being left records scroll 0. At head the code is unchanged: `if (content.current) content.current.scrollTop = 0;` runs before `onLocation?.(next)`. useExplorerNavigation.enter calls remember(leaving), which reads `pane?.scrollTop` of `.metaproject-content` (PANES index CONTENT_PANE) at that moment. The content ref in OpenSpecView is that same element (`<section ref={content} className="metaproject-content"`). The T8 dispatch listed OpenSpecView.tsx among its target_files, but nothing in slice-03 shows this item was taken or declined.
finding.impact: Back to a previous OpenSpec entry returns to the top of its document, not where the reader was. This is a silent wrong restore, not data loss, and AC11 covers only Graph selections.
finding.suggested_fix: In choose(), do not reset scrollTop before onLocation; let navigate(..., { resetContent: true }) seed the new entry at 0 (the hook already supports it), or record the offsets before zeroing. Or record the item as accepted in the journal.
finding.evidence: First recorded by the T7 worker under noticed_not_touched (results/T7.result.json); review-architecture (wave 2) pointed at the same record. finding.problem: T9 dispatch names files as existing that are absent at head, and requires a result file the journal says was not requested. T9.dispatch.json has context_refs entry `resolved/T9.implement.json` with "exists": true and output_contract.artifact_path `results/T9.result.json`, and a constraint to validate that result against the resolved file. Neither file is in the flow folder at head (resolved/ holds T5-T8, T12-T14, T16; results/ holds T5-T8, T12-T14, T16), and git history has no record of them. The journal entry for T9 says "No result JSON was requested for this docs task", which contradicts the dispatch. T15 (also docs, flow.json status done) has no result or resolved file either. flow.json marks both T9 and T15 done with disposition completed.
finding.impact: A gate input that says a file exists when it does not, and a done task with no result artifact, mean a later reader or the review-flow gate cannot check T9 and T15 against the contract the dispatch states; the evidence is only the journal prose.
finding.suggested_fix: Either record in flow.json dispositionReason for T9 and T15 that the docs workers returned inline and no result artifact exists, or remove the stale context_refs entry and output_contract from T9.dispatch.json. Do not edit flow.json by hand; use the keryx flow CLI.

finding.quote: if (edge.from === projection.root) adjacent.outgoing.push({ edge, node: to });
finding.problem: The panel counts and lists a self-loop edge (edge.from === edge.to === root) once, as outgoing (documented in groupRelationships). The graph layout skips self-loops (`if (edge.from === edge.to) return;` in layoutNeighborhood), so its caption count leaves them out. The two numbers are computed from the same projection for the same selection and shown on one screen.
finding.impact: For a node with a self-edge (for example a wiki page whose `links` edge points at itself) the graph caption reads '0 incoming · 0 outgoing' while the panel fact reads '0 incoming · 1 outgoing', and the Relationships tab lists the node as its own outgoing neighbour, whose row selects the node already shown (a no-op). AC7 asks for the panel counts to come from the root-adjacent edges, so the panel follows the criterion; the caption is the one that differs.
finding.suggested_fix: Pick one rule for both: skip self-loops in groupRelationships (the row does nothing useful), or count them in layoutNeighborhood. Skipping them in groupRelationships keeps the two counts equal.
finding.evidence: RelationshipList.tsx groupRelationships: `if (edge.from === projection.root) adjacent.outgoing.push(...)` runs before any self-loop test; graphLayout.ts lines 505-508: `if (edge.from === edge.to) return; if (edge.to === root.id) incoming++; if (edge.from === root.id) outgoing++;`. The self-loop case is only reachable if the producer emits a self-edge; not verified that it does.

known_findings.problem: The explorer root `<section className="flows metaproject">` becomes a size container. container-type inline-size applies layout containment, and an element with layout containment is the containing block of its `position: fixed` descendants. The Filters popover (`FiltersPopover` in MetaprojectView.tsx, rendered inside that section, class `menu`, which `styles.css` sets to `position: fixed`) is placed with viewport coordinates from `anchor.getBoundingClientRect()` (`left`, `top: rect.bottom + 4`). With the new container, those values are resolved against the section's padding box, not the viewport, so the popover is shifted by the section's own viewport offset (sidebar width, toolbar height) and the Escape/outside-press logic and the horizontal clamp to `window.innerWidth` no longer match where it is drawn.

The G8 test reads graph.css from disk and matches a regex over its text, including the exact declaration `min-block-size: 200px;`. It verifies the stylesheet's spelling, not that the graph fills its host, and it will fail on any harmless reformat or a change of the minimum (the T8 notes lower the minimum to 160px in a narrow container, done in metaproject.css).

known_findings.quote: it served the committed MetaprojectView.tsx for the few seconds of the red check
known_findings.problem: Red checks swapped tracked source files in the shared worktree under a live dev server

RetainedView is a generic view-retention helper exported from the composition root. `export function RetainedView({ active, visible, children })` lives in App.tsx and is exported only so App.dom.test.tsx can import it (`(await import("./App")).RetainedView`). The component has no dependency on App state; the existing session/flows/issues views still use the inline `hidden={view !== ...}` pattern, so two retention idioms now coexist in one file. This is a placement opinion, not a violation of a named rule.

isOpenSpecNode is exported but has no importer outside its own file. `export const isOpenSpecNode` is used only inside NodeDetailsPanel.tsx (line 87); the keryx ctx rg search over apps/desktop/src found no other import. The plan's interface section lists it as an export, which explains it, so this is a note on a public surface nobody consumes.

`back` reads `previousRoutes.current`, which is refreshed from `history` only on render, while `enter` updates `current.current` eagerly but not `previousRoutes.current`. Two calls in one event tick, `navigate`/`visit` then `back`, would pop the entry before the one just pushed.

Narrow-host container rule for the docked panel looks unreachable (unverified). This rule sits inside `@container metaproject (max-width: 760px)` and matches only while the panel is docked (not .compact). NodeDetailsPanel.tsx sets compact when `availableWidth < COMPACT_BELOW` (820, lines 11 and 154). If availableWidth is the width of the panes area, it is not wider than the .metaproject container, so a docked panel implies a container of about 820 px or more, outside the 760 px query, and the narrower 150-180 px list column may never apply.
